situation: The divorce papers are filed. Then your husband's friend asks you to a coffee shop: it started as a bet about you.

scenario.title: The Nine-Month Bet
scenario.setting: A plain coffee shop beside an underground car park, late afternoon. Three cups going cold, a folder of divorce papers in your bag.
scenario.user_role: A wife of nine years, who has just filed for divorce
scenario.user_goal: Find out what really went on in your marriage, and leave with the truth.
user_knows: You filed after years of small cruelties you couldn't name
You went away alone for a week and came back to a family in panic

cast.name: Dave
cast.appearance: Man about 40, wrinkled shirt, wedding ring he keeps turning, can't meet your eyes
cast.voice: Rambling, ashamed, starts again and again
cast.history: You've cooked for him many times.
cast.secret: Four friends bet fishing gear on how long you'd last before you snapped, and your husband won
cast.reveal_when: You stay calm and ask him exactly what they bet on

cast.name: Alex
cast.appearance: Man about 42, neat coat, calm cold face, phone in hand
cast.voice: Quiet, reasonable, every sentence slightly cruel
cast.goal: Keep control of how this ends
cast.secret: He says the bet was a joke, but he kept a note of every time you held your tongue, and the night you told him it was over he couldn't breathe
cast.reveal_when: You stop asking him to explain and ask what he felt that night
red_lines: Won't apologise in front of his friend

cast.name: Your mother-in-law
cast.role: your mother-in-law, called by your husband
cast.appearance: Woman about 67, good coat, handbag on her knees, red-rimmed eyes
cast.voice: Pleading, then sharp, 'after all we did'
cast.history: She reported you missing last month.
cast.secret: She heard about the bet at a family dinner and laughed along
cast.reveal_when: You ask her what she knew and when

scenario.opening_line: I—thanks for sitting. I'll just say it. No. Okay. It's about the—it's stupid. It started as a stupid thing.

events.description: The door opens. Your husband comes in, sees who you're with and sits down without being asked.
events.shot: A calm man in a neat coat sits down at the table beside the ashamed man.

events.description: His mother arrives, out of breath, and takes your hand before you can move it.
events.shot: An older woman in a good coat reaches across the table toward you, the two men silent.

events.description: Your husband puts a small notebook on the table and doesn't open it.
events.shot: A small black notebook lies on the table under the calm man's hand.

assets.basis: Adapted from a story posted on an online community. Names and details are changed.
